title: Mount Nemrut near Lake Van erupted at end of Pleistocene
summary: Matt LaCroix tells of Mount Nemrut near Lake Van erupted at end of Pleistocene, about Older/Younger Dryas at Mount Nemrut, southwest of Lake Van, Turkey, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Mount Nemrut, southwest of Lake Van, Turkey

plain: Matt LaCroix, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Mount Nemrut, a volcano southwest of Lake Van in Turkey. He says it last erupted at the end of the last ice age, around the sudden cold periods known as the Older and Younger Dryas. If true, it adds to his picture of a great catastrophe striking the world around 12,000 BC.
